verses.text: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.

xrefs.text: But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
Now the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you just as I was with Moses.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
“May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation

verses.text: Now they sin more and more and make for themselves cast images, idols skillfully made from their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. People say of them, “They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!”

xrefs.text: They pour out their bags of gold and weigh out silver on scales; they hire a goldsmith to fashion it into a god, so they can bow down and worship.
Nevertheless, I have reserved seven thousand in Israel— all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.”
From the rest he makes a god, his graven image. He bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, “Save me, for you are my god.”
They adorn it with silver and gold and fasten it with hammer and nails, so that it will not totter.
For she does not acknowledge that it was I who gave her grain, new wine, and oil, who lavished on her silver and gold— which they crafted for Baal.

verses.text: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, like smoke through an open window.

xrefs.text: Not so the wicked! For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.
As smoke is blown away, You will drive them out; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish in the presence of God.
What shall I do with you, O Ephraim What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.
The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.

Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered and became like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

verses.text: Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me.

xrefs.text: Speak up and present your case— yes, let them take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago? Who announced it from ancient times? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me.
“I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.

“You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen, so that you may consider and believe Me and understand that I am He. Before Me no god was formed, and after Me none will come.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I give Egypt for your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.

verses.text: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.

xrefs.text: He found him in a desert land, in a barren, howling wilderness; He surrounded him, He instructed him, He guarded him as the apple of His eye.

Indeed, the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing.
He led you through the vast and terrifying wilderness with its venomous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty and waterless land. He brought you water from the rock of flint.
But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
Although my spirit grows faint within me, You know my way. Along the path I travel they have hidden a snare for me.

verses.text: When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me.

xrefs.text: He made him ride on the heights of the land and fed him the produce of the field. He nourished him with honey from the rock and oil from the flinty crag,
Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses in which to dwell,
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that He would give you— a land with great and splendid cities that you did not build,
You ignored the Rock who brought you forth; you forgot the God who gave you birth.
In his pride the wicked man does not seek Him; in all his schemes there is no God.

verses.text: So like a lion I will pounce on them; like a leopard I will lurk by the path.

xrefs.text: Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will ravage them. A leopard will lie in wait near their cities, and everyone who ventures out will be torn to pieces. For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous.
For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.
He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush.
He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”
Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?

verses.text: Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them, and I will tear open their chests. There I will devour them like a lion, like a wild beast tearing them apart.

xrefs.text: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away, and no one can rescue it.

I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said: “Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Topple them on the heads of all the people, and I will kill the rest with the sword. None of those who flee will get away; none of the fugitives will escape.
Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you:
It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.

verses.text: You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me— against your helper.

xrefs.text: Have you not brought this on yourself by forsaking the LORD your God when He led you in the way?

Your own evil will discipline you; your own apostasies will reprimand you. Consider and realize how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of Me,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
“There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your aid, and the clouds in His majesty.
He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.
Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty.

verses.text: Where is your king now to save you in all your cities, and the rulers to whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?

xrefs.text: They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval. With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction.
“Look,” they said, “you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.”
Surely now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD. What can a king do for us?”
On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth— the LORD alone, and His name alone.
He will say: “Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,

verses.text: So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.

xrefs.text: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans.”
A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.

Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”
So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

verses.text: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.

xrefs.text: “Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?
My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.

verses.text: Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, he fails to present himself at the opening of the womb.

xrefs.text: to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.
As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain, so were we in Your presence, O LORD.

Why do you now cry aloud? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor perished so that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?

verses.text: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting? Compassion is hidden from My eyes.

xrefs.text: He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of His people from the whole earth. For the LORD has spoken.
in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.
But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah
Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

verses.text: Although he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come— a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry. The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.

xrefs.text: But it was uprooted in fury, cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped off and they withered; the fire consumed them.
Even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem, “A searing wind from the barren heights in the desert blows toward the daughter of My people, but not to winnow or to sift;
And the second son he named Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

But his father refused. “I know, my son, I know!” he said. “He too shall become a people, and he too shall be great; nevertheless, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.”

verses.text: Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.

xrefs.text: “Why is my lord weeping?” asked Hazael. “Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites,” Elisha replied. “You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little ones to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
At that time Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacked Tiphsah and everyone in its vicinity, because they would not open their gates. So he attacked Tiphsah and ripped open all the pregnant women.
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives will be ravished.
O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.

This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of the Ammonites, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.
